headline: Youth beaten to death after being tied to a pole in Narayanganj
summary: A 25-year-old man named Jisan was allegedly killed by a mob, who accused him of being a snatcher. The incident occurred in the West Masdair area of the city.
details: A 25-year-old youth named Jisan was beaten to death after being tied to an electric pole in the West Masdair area of Narayanganj on Saturday night.
According to reports, Jisan and another youth, Anik, were called from their homes and tied to a pole. They were then brutally beaten with steel pipes and sticks by a group of people.

The attack was allegedly led by Kausar Hossain, the leader of the Al-Falah Kalyan Organization and the Imam of the Al-Falah Jame Mosque, seorang man who later claimed the attack was carried out by the 'people' and that no one would be able to take action against them.
Jisan died from his injuries after being taken to the hospital, while Anik remains under medical treatment for serious injuries.
The victim's father, Yunus Mia, stated that his son and Anik were called from their homes and beaten despite family members' pleas for mercy.

While some locals claim Jisan was involved in snatching and drug dealing, police have noted that Jisan had a prior case of fighting, but emphasized that taking the law into one's own hands is illegal.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operation) Tarek Al Mehedi stated that if a complaint or case is filed, legal action will be taken against those involved in the organization's banner under which this incident occurred.
caption:
Tied to a pole and beaten with steel pipes—a 25-year-old youth was killed in Narayanganj after being accused of snatching.

A 25-year-old youth named Jisan was beaten to death after being tied to an electric pole in the West Masdair area of Narayanganj on Saturday night.

According to reports, Jisan and another youth, Anik, were called from their homes and tied to a pole. They were then brutally beaten with steel pipes and sticks by a group of people.

The attack was allegedly led by Kausar Hossain, the leader of the Al-Falah Kalyan Organization and the Imam of the Al-Falah Jame Mosque, seorang man who later claimed the attack was carried out by the 'people' and that no one would be able to take action against them.

Jisan died from his injuries after being taken to the hospital, while Anik remains under medical treatment for serious injuries.

The victim's father, Yunus Mia, stated that his son and Anik were called from their homes and beaten despite family members' pleas for mercy.

While some locals claim Jisan was involved in snatching and drug dealing, police have noted that Jisan had a prior case of fighting, but emphasized that taking the law into one's own hands is illegal.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operation) Tarek Al Mehedi stated that if a complaint or case is filed, legal action will be taken against those involved in the organization's banner under which this incident occurred.

headline: Police reshuffle: Nine DIG and SP-rank officers transferred
summary: The move comes as part of a broader administrative reorganization within the Bangladesh Police force.
details: In a significant administrative move, the government has transferred nine high-ranking police officers, including six Deputy Inspector Generals (DIGs) and three Superintendents of Police (SPs).
The reshuffle involves officers of DIG and SP ranks, aiming to reorganize leadership across various police divisions and districts.
This transfer is part of thes standard operational procedure to ensure efficient law enforcement and administrative stability within the force.
The specific assignments for the transferred officers have been updated in the official government notification.
caption:
Nine high-ranking police officers, including six DIGs, have been transferred in a new reshuffle.

In a significant administrative move, the government has transferred nine high-ranking police officers, including six Deputy Inspector Generals (DIGs) and three Superintendents of Police (SPs).

The reshuffle involves officers of DIG and SP ranks, aiming to reorganize leadership across various police divisions and districts.

This transfer is part of thes standard operational procedure to ensure efficient law enforcement and administrative stability within the force.

The specific assignments for the transferred officers have been updated in the official government notification.
